title: Signing out during a sign-in renewal stays signed out
owns: app/main/agent/auth.ts, the keeper and sign-out wiring in app/main/main.ts

items.title: Signing out while a startup renewal is in flight is undone: the renewed sign-in is saved again and Ember reconnects with it
items.scenario: Ember's own GitHub App token is stored and ran out overnight, so the next start renews it before use. startBrain (main.ts ~1985) awaits keeper.freshen(), and findToken (Check again, the GitHub CLI wait) does the same. freshen() sends the refresh_token request. While that request is out, the user clicks Sign out in settings, which opens at a normal start. The IPC.signOut handler (main.ts 1215-1226) calls tokens.clear(), sets currentToken = null, calls keeper.use(null) and agent.start(null). Then GitHub answers. freshen() then calls store.saveAsync(next) without checking that the sign-in it renewed is still the one stored: it writes the renewed grant back to github-token.bin and sets it as held. startBrain goes on to resolveToken(tokens, ...), which now returns the resurrected token with source "stored", and connectWith(found, "auto") calls agent.start with it. host.start's signedOut flag only blocks environment and GitHub CLI tokens, so the stored one connects. The user is signed back in to the account they just left, and its token is on disk for every later start. A related case: when the renewal request is slow (a connection stuck across a network change) and the user signs in with the device flow as another account meanwhile, freshen's save overwrites the new account's grant, and startBrain then switches Copilot to the old account. The device-flow handler's comment says a renewal finishing meanwhile is "neither switched to nor saved". That holds for GrantKeeper.renew(), which checks this.grant and inUse, but not for freshen().
items.evidence: I reproduced it with a scratch test, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/relfix3-review/safety/tree/test/unit/zz-safety-signout.test.ts (run with `npx vitest run test/unit/zz-safety-signout.test.ts` in that tree). It stores an expired grant, starts keeper.freshen() with a fetch held open, then calls store.clear() and keeper.use(null) as sign-out does, then lets the fetch answer. Output: `SCRATCH after sign-out, saved: false`, then `SCRATCH after the renewal finished, saved: true token: ghu_bb`, then `SCRATCH resolveToken after sign-out: stored true`. In the code, freshen() (auth.ts 517-535) does `const next = await this.renewed(g); const kept = await store.saveAsync(next);` with no turn, epoch or stored-token check after the await. saveAsync takes its epoch only when it is called, after clear(), so the epoch guard doesn't help. renew() (auth.ts 588-605) does have `if (this.grant !== grant || this.d.inUse() !== grant.token) return;`.
items.fix: In freshen(), note the keeper's turn (or a store generation such as TokenStore.epoch) before renewing. After `await this.renewed(g)`, save only if no use(), stop(), clear() or save happened meanwhile and the store still holds g.token (re-read it with loadGrant). Otherwise drop the renewed grant, or revoke it. In main.ts startBrain and findToken, don't connect with a "stored" token when a sign-out happened after the look began (check agent signedOut state, or a sign-out counter, after freshen and resolveToken).
